discovery: Semiconductor quantum-dot sources of single and indistinguishable photons on demand
motivation: In 2000 Michler, İmamoğlu and co-workers showed that a single semiconductor quantum dot in a microcavity emits triggered single photons, turning an artificial atom in a solid into a deterministic quantum light source. Yamamoto's group then demonstrated triggered single photons and, in 2002, indistinguishable photons from a quantum dot, the property needed for two-photon interference and linear-optics quantum information. These experiments established solid-state quantum emitters as practical, electrically and optically addressable sources that can be grown, nanofabricated and integrated on chips. Today quantum-dot sources achieve near-unity purity, high indistinguishability and high brightness. They power boson-sampling and photonic quantum-computing demonstrations, entangled-photon generation, quantum key distribution and quantum networks, and are sold commercially. This work transformed nonclassical light from a laboratory curiosity into a reliable technology, opening an entire field of solid-state quantum photonics.
